elements: Operating a motor vehicle
Upon a highway or other place open to the general public
While under the influence of alcoholic liquor OR with BAC of 0.08% or more
enhancements: BAC 0.17%+ (Super Drunk/High BAC): 180 days jail, $700 fine — MCL 257.625(1)(c)
Child under 16 in vehicle: additional 93-day misdemeanor charge — MCL 257.625(7)
Prior OWI within 7 years: second offense felony
notes: Michigan uses 'Operating While Intoxicated' (OWI), not DUI/DWI. License suspension 30-180 days. Mandatory vehicle immobilization. Ignition interlock may be required.

elements: Operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated
Prior conviction for OWI, OWVI, or OUIN within 7 years
mandatory_minimum: 5 days jail or 30 days community service
enhancements: Third offense within 10 years: Class E Felony
BAC 0.17%+ on second offense: enhanced penalties
Child in vehicle at time of offense: additional charges
notes: License revocation minimum 1 year. Vehicle immobilization 90-180 days. Ignition interlock required upon reinstatement.

statute_title: Operating While Intoxicated — Third or Subsequent Offense
elements: Operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated
Two or more prior OWI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 30 days jail or 60 days community service
enhancements: Prior felony OWI conviction: enhanced sentencing
Serious injury resulting: Class D Felony — MCL 257.625(5)
Death resulting: Class B Felony — MCL 257.625(4)
notes: License revocation. Vehicle forfeiture possible. Habitual offender provisions apply.

statute_title: Operating While Intoxicated by Controlled Substance
elements: Operating a motor vehicle
While under the influence of a controlled substance
OR with any amount of a Schedule 1 controlled substance in blood (per se rule)
enhancements: Prior OWI within 7 years: second offense penalties
Death resulting: Class B Felony
notes: Michigan has a zero-tolerance per se law for any Schedule 1 controlled substance or cocaine in blood regardless of impairment (OUIN — Operating with presence of drugs). Separate from impairment-based OWI.

statute_title: Operating While Intoxicated Causing Serious Impairment of a Body Function
elements: Operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated
Causing an accident
Resulting in serious impairment of a body function of another person
enhancements: Prior OWI record: consecutive sentencing possible
Death caused: Class B Felony — MCL 257.625(4)
notes: 'Serious impairment' defined as substantial limitation of important body function. License revocation.

elements: Operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated
Causing the death of another person
enhancements: Emergency responder killed: enhanced sentencing
Multiple deaths: consecutive sentences per victim
notes: License revocation. Vehicle forfeiture. Also known as 'OWI Causing Death.' Prosecutors may also charge second-degree murder if egregious facts.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (up to 93 days for first; 6 months for injury)
elements: Operating a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
enhancements: Causing serious injury: up to 2 years — MCL 257.626b
Causing death: up to 15 years — MCL 257.626b
notes: 6 points on driving record. License suspension possible. Distinguished from careless driving (civil infraction).

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended, Revoked, or Denied
penalty_max: 93 days first offense; 1 year second offense
elements: Operating a motor vehicle upon a highway
While operator's license is suspended, revoked, denied, or never obtained
enhancements: Second offense within 7 years: 1-year misdemeanor
OWI-related suspension: enhanced penalties
Third or subsequent: possible felony
notes: Vehicle may be immobilized. Prior OWI-related suspension adds additional penalties.

penalty_max: Misdemeanor penalties for violations over MRTMA limits
elements: Possession of marijuana
In excess of 2.5 ounces in public or 10 ounces at home
OR transfer to minor
enhancements: Possession near school: additional penalties
Transfer to minor: Class E or D Felony — MCL 333.7401c
notes: Adult recreational marijuana is legal in Michigan under MRTMA (MCL 333.27951 et seq.) up to 2.5 oz publicly, 10 oz at home. Exceedances are civil infractions or misdemeanors depending on amount. Medical use governed by MMMA.

elements: Knowing possession
Of a controlled substance
Not authorized by law
enhancements: Possession of 25+ grams heroin/cocaine: possession with intent presumed
Prior drug conviction: additional sentencing points
In drug-free school zone: double penalties
notes: Michigan Sentencing Guidelines apply. First-time offenders may be eligible for Holmes Youthful Trainee Act (HYTA) or 7411 deferral. Drug courts widely available.

offense_class: Class A-E Felony (varies by substance and amount)
elements: Delivery, manufacture, or possession with intent to deliver
A controlled substance
Knowingly and intentionally
mandatory_minimum: Varies by quantity; life for 1,000+ grams cocaine/heroin
enhancements: 1,000+ grams cocaine/heroin: life or any term of years — Class A
450-999 grams: up to 30 years — Class B
50-449 grams: up to 20 years — Class C
25-49 grams: up to 4 years — Class E
Delivery to minor: double penalty — MCL 333.7410
In drug-free school zone: 2-year mandatory consecutive — MCL 333.7410a
notes: Michigan's drug trafficking law has quantity-based tiers. Large-scale trafficking carries life sentences. 'Delivery' includes constructive transfer.

elements: Delivery or manufacture of a controlled substance
1,000 or more grams of mixture containing cocaine, heroin, or methamphetamine
Knowingly and intentionally
mandatory_minimum: Life or any term of years (judicial discretion within Class A)
enhancements: Prior drug felony: enhanced minimum
Use of firearm: consecutive penalty — MCL 750.227b
Leadership role: sentencing enhancement
notes: Highest drug trafficking tier. Federal prosecution often pursued concurrently. Asset forfeiture applies.

elements: Manufacturing methamphetamine
Or possessing precursor chemicals with intent to manufacture
Knowingly and intentionally
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of minor: additional 2-year consecutive — MCL 333.7401d
Manufacturing causing injury: aggravated charges
Prior conviction: sentencing enhancement
notes: Separate offense for meth labs. Environmental cleanup liability. Methamphetamine lab in presence of minor is standalone offense under MCL 333.7401d.

elements: Possession of drug paraphernalia
With intent to use in connection with controlled substance violation
enhancements: Sale of paraphernalia to minor: misdemeanor — MCL 333.7453
Combination with possession charge: consecutive possible
notes: Michigan's paraphernalia statute is part of the Public Health Code. Items must have drug-related purpose.

elements: Killing of a human being
With premeditation and deliberation
OR during perpetration of an enumerated felony (felony murder)
enhancements: Victim is law enforcement: LWOP mandatory
Multiple victims: consecutive LWOP terms
Juvenile offenders: Miller v. Alabama applies — individualized sentencing
notes: Michigan abolished the death penalty in 1847. LWOP is the maximum. Felony murder (during robbery, CSC, arson, etc.) also first degree. Juveniles subject to Miller hearing.

penalty_min: Life or any term of years
elements: Killing of a human being
With malice aforethought
Without premeditation or during non-enumerated felony
enhancements: Prior murder conviction: life mandatory
Use of firearm: 2-year mandatory consecutive — MCL 750.227b
Gang-related: sentencing enhancement
notes: Includes depraved heart murder. No death penalty in Michigan. 'Malice aforethought' can be implied from circumstances. Sentencing allows judge discretion on term.

elements: Killing of a human being
Without malice
In the heat of passion caused by adequate provocation
Before cooling off
enhancements: Use of firearm: 2-year consecutive minimum — MCL 750.227b
Prior violent felony: sentencing enhancement
Domestic victim: aggravating factor
notes: Michigan manslaughter statute is general. Heat of passion must be reasonable. Cooling off period negates defense.

elements: Killing of a human being
By pointing or aiming a firearm
Without intent to kill
enhancements: Gross negligence (without firearm): common law manslaughter
OWI causing death: separate MCL 257.625(4)
notes: MCL 750.329 specifically covers firearm-related involuntary manslaughter. General negligent manslaughter is common law in Michigan. Vehicular manslaughter prosecuted under OWI statute.

elements: An act intended to cause harmful or offensive contact
OR an attempt to commit battery
Against another person
enhancements: Domestic violence: 93-day misdemeanor (same statute, different track)
Second DV offense: 1-year misdemeanor — MCL 750.81(4)
Third DV offense: Class E Felony — MCL 750.81(5)
notes: Michigan combines assault and battery into one offense. Simple assault is the uncompleted act; battery is the completed touching. Both charged under MCL 750.81.

statute_title: Assault — Infliction of Serious or Aggravated Injury
elements: Assault or battery
Infliction of a serious or aggravated injury
Without a weapon
enhancements: Against pregnant woman: Class E Felony — MCL 750.81d(3)
Against utility/transit worker: Class E Felony
Strangulation: Class D Felony (up to 10 years) — MCL 750.84(1)(b)
notes: Serious injury without a weapon. More severe charges apply with weapons or specific victims. Strangulation is separately enhanced under MCL 750.84.

statute_title: Felonious Assault (Assault with a Dangerous Weapon)
elements: An assault
With a dangerous weapon
Without intending to commit murder or great bodily harm
enhancements: With intent to murder or do great bodily harm: AWIGBH — Class D Felony — MCL 750.84
In weapon-free school zone: additional 2-year consecutive — MCL 750.82(2)
Against law enforcement: enhanced felony
notes: 'Dangerous weapon' broadly construed — includes vehicles, glass bottles, dogs. AWIGBH under MCL 750.84 is more serious (Class D, up to 10 years).

elements: In the course of committing a larceny
Use of force or violence against any person
OR putting person in fear of immediate force or violence
enhancements: Armed robbery (dangerous weapon): Class B Felony — MCL 750.529
Carjacking: Class A Felony — MCL 750.529a
Victim injury: sentencing enhancement
Use of firearm: 2-year consecutive — MCL 750.227b
notes: Unarmed robbery. Michigan requires force 'in the course of committing' — includes immediately before or after larceny. Armed robbery carries up to life under MCL 750.529.

elements: Robbery
While armed with a dangerous weapon
OR while representing oneself to be armed
mandatory_minimum: 2-year consecutive for firearm use under MCL 750.227b
enhancements: Carjacking (armed): Class A Felony up to life — MCL 750.529a
Victim seriously injured: increased sentence
Gang involvement: sentencing enhancement
notes: Carrying or claiming to have a weapon both qualify. Firearm possession charge runs consecutive under 750.227b. Carjacking is distinct and more severe.

penalty_min: Life or any term of years
elements: Knowingly restraining another person
With intent to hold for ransom, use as shield/hostage, engage in criminal sexual conduct, inflict bodily injury, terrorize, or interfere with governmental functions
OR secret confinement
enhancements: Victim is minor: presumptive life
Death of victim: LWOP or life
Crossing state lines: federal prosecution likely
notes: MCL 750.349b covers 'unlawful imprisonment' as lesser offense (Class D). Secret confinement kidnapping unique to Michigan. Jury must be instructed on lesser.

penalty_min: Life or any term of years
elements: In the course of committing a larceny of a motor vehicle
Use or threat of force or violence against the person
Or putting person in fear
enhancements: Armed with firearm: 2-year consecutive — MCL 750.227b
Victim injury: sentencing enhancement
Vehicle used in crime: additional charges
notes: Separate from armed robbery. Specific to motor vehicle taking. Can be charged alongside other offenses arising from same conduct.

elements: Breaking and entering any building, tent, hotel, office, store, or other structure
With intent to commit a felony or larceny therein
enhancements: Home invasion (dwelling): Class B or C Felony — MCL 750.110a
Armed: additional firearm penalty
Prior B&E conviction: sentencing enhancement
notes: Michigan uses 'Breaking and Entering' rather than burglary. Home invasion is more severe. Constructive breaking (entering through open door with intent) is sufficient.

statute_title: Home Invasion — First, Second, Third Degree
offense_class: Class B Felony (1st degree); Class C Felony (2nd); Class D Felony (3rd)
elements: Breaking and entering a dwelling
OR entering without permission
With intent to commit felony, larceny, or assault while therein
1st degree: armed with dangerous weapon or another person present
enhancements: Victim injured during home invasion: enhanced sentencing
Armed: additional 2-year consecutive — MCL 750.227b
Prior home invasion: sentencing enhancement
notes: Three degrees based on aggravating factors. First degree is the most serious — armed or occupied dwelling. Occupied dwelling home invasion is Class B (up to 20 years).

elements: Taking and carrying away
Property of another person
With intent to permanently deprive the owner of the property
enhancements: $20,000+: Class F Felony (up to 5 years) — MCL 750.356(4)(a)
From a person (larceny from person): Class G Felony — MCL 750.357
Habitual offender: enhanced sentencing
Organized retail theft: additional charges — MCL 752.1084
notes: Michigan larceny is threshold-based: <$200 (93-day), $200-$1,000 (1 year), $1,000-$20,000 (Class H/5 years), $20,000+ (Class F/10 years). Note: thresholds raised 2024.

elements: Taking or using a motor vehicle
Without authority of owner
With intent to steal or permanently deprive
enhancements: Carjacking (force used): Class A Felony — MCL 750.529a
Prior auto theft: sentencing enhancement
Organized auto theft ring: enhanced charges — MCL 750.535a
notes: Michigan uses 'Taking Motor Vehicle Without Authority' (TMVA). Joyriding (temporary use without permission) is a separate misdemeanor under MCL 750.414.

statute_title: Retail Fraud — First, Second, Third Degree
elements: While in a store in which goods are offered for sale
Altering price, concealing goods, or removing merchandise
With intent to steal or pay less than the full price
enhancements: Organized retail fraud: Class F Felony — MCL 752.1084
Fraud device/tool used: enhanced charge
Prior retail fraud conviction: degree enhancement
notes: Retail fraud degrees based on value: 1st ($1,000+, felony), 2nd ($200-$1,000), 3rd (under $200). Michigan-specific terminology. Civil demand for damages also possible.

statute_title: Arson — Burning of a Dwelling House
penalty_min: Life or any term of years
elements: Willful and malicious burning
Of a dwelling house
Whether occupied or not
enhancements: Person present and injured: aggravated arson
Firefighter injured: enhanced penalty
Insurance fraud arson: additional fraud charges
notes: Burning a dwelling is the most serious arson. MCL 750.73 (burning real property, non-dwelling) is Class D. MCL 750.74 (burning personal property) is Class E-H.

elements: Wilfully and maliciously
Destroying, injuring, or damaging
Property of another person
enhancements: Religious institution: mandatory minimum applies — MCL 750.377b
School property: enhanced — MCL 380.1300
Graffiti: separate civil liability
notes: Michigan's vandalism/property damage statute uses value thresholds same as larceny. Restitution mandatory. Bias-motivated MDOP subject to ethnic intimidation enhancement.

elements: Assault or assault and battery
Against a person who is a spouse, former spouse, dating partner, or co-habitant
OR parent of a common child
enhancements: Strangulation: Class D Felony — MCL 750.84(1)(b)
Aggravated DV (serious injury): 1-year or Class E Felony
Violation of PPO: contempt or criminal charge
notes: Michigan tracks DV offenses separately for enhancement purposes. Third conviction creates felony regardless of severity. Mandatory arrest policy in most jurisdictions. Firearm prohibition upon conviction.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1 year); Class E Felony if aggravated
elements: A willful course of conduct
Involving repeated or continuing harassment of another individual
That would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, or harassed
enhancements: Aggravated stalking (violation of PPO, prior conviction, under 18 victim): Class E Felony — MCL 750.411i
Cyberstalking: same statute applies to electronic communications
Victim safety plan violation: additional penalties
notes: Michigan's cyberstalking provisions include electronic communications, emails, and social media. 'Course of conduct' requires at least 2 acts.

elements: Existence of a Personal Protection Order
Respondent had knowledge of the order
Conduct prohibited by the order occurred
enhancements: Second violation: 1-year misdemeanor
Assault during violation: separate felony charges
Criminal contempt proceedings also available: up to 93 days
notes: Michigan PPOs are civil orders enforced criminally. Violation triggers both criminal prosecution and contempt. Armed respondents subject to federal gun prohibition.

statute_title: Child Abuse — First Through Fourth Degree
offense_class: Class B Felony (1st); Class D Felony (2nd); Class G Felony (3rd); Misdemeanor (4th)
elements: Intentionally or knowingly causing physical harm to a child
OR cruel punishment/torture (1st degree)
OR omission causing harm (2nd-4th degree)
mandatory_minimum: None (1st degree life or any term)
enhancements: Child death resulting: murder charges
Pattern of abuse: sentencing enhancement
Prior child abuse conviction: enhanced degree
notes: Michigan has four degrees of child abuse. 1st degree (Life) requires intent to cause serious physical harm or torture. Mandatory reporters include all adults in Michigan under MCL 722.623.

statute_title: Child Neglect / Failure to Provide — Criminal
offense_class: Misdemeanor to Class E Felony (depends on harm)
penalty_max: 2 years (if serious harm); otherwise 93 days to 1 year
elements: Parent, guardian, or person with legal custody
Fails to provide adequate food, clothing, shelter, or medical care
To a child under age 18
enhancements: Serious physical harm results: Class E Felony
Death of child: murder or manslaughter
Prior CPS history: sentencing enhancement
notes: Criminal neglect separate from CPS/civil neglect proceedings. Both may run concurrently. Child endangerment also charged under MCL 750.136b(4th degree).

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Felon (PFWDVRO)
elements: Possession or use of a firearm
By a person convicted of a specified felony
Within the specified period after completing sentence
enhancements: Certain violent felony prior: lifetime ban
Federal prosecution concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)
Use in crime: additional charges
notes: Michigan's felon-in-possession applies for 3 years after completion of sentence for specified felonies (firearms, CSC, etc.), or permanently for violent felonies. Different from federal lifetime ban.

elements: Carrying a pistol concealed on person
OR in a vehicle
Without a valid Concealed Pistol License (CPL)
enhancements: Prior felony: sentence enhancement
In weapon-free school zone: additional 2-year consecutive
Used in crime: additional charges
notes: Michigan is a shall-issue CPL state. CPL holders exempt. Open carry of pistol in vehicle without CPL is still unlawful under MCL 750.227. Separate provisions for long guns.

statute_title: Felony Firearm — Possession During Commission of Felony
elements: Carrying or having in possession a firearm
At the time of commission or attempt of a felony
Regardless of whether the firearm was used
enhancements: Second felony firearm offense: 5-year mandatory consecutive
Third felony firearm offense: life imprisonment
No parole/probation on mandatory term
notes: Michigan's felony firearm statute is extremely powerful — mandatory consecutive sentence cannot be suspended or paroled. Simply possessing firearm during felony triggers it. Most influential Michigan gun law in practice.

statute_title: Assault with a Firearm (Felonious Assault + Felony Firearm)
penalty_max: 4 years (felonious assault) + 2 years mandatory consecutive (felony firearm)
elements: Felonious assault with firearm as dangerous weapon
PLUS: possession of firearm at time of felony
mandatory_minimum: 2 years consecutive mandatory for felony firearm component
enhancements: Intent to kill: assault with intent to murder — MCL 750.83
Great bodily harm: AWIGBH — MCL 750.84
Law enforcement victim: enhanced penalties
notes: In practice, assault with firearm charges are filed as both MCL 750.82 (felonious assault) and MCL 750.227b (felony firearm). The 2-year mandatory runs consecutive.

offense_class: Class F Felony (information theft); Class E Felony (financial harm)
penalty_max: 5 years (identity theft); additional up to 5 years for use
elements: Obtaining personal identifying information of another
Without authorization
With intent to fraudulently use to obtain money, credit, goods, services, or other property
enhancements: Elderly victim: sentencing enhancement
Multiple victims: consecutive charges
Financial losses over $20,000: Class D Felony
notes: Michigan Identity Theft Protection Act (MCL 445.61 et seq.). Both identity theft (obtaining information) and identity fraud (using information) are separate offenses. Restitution mandatory.

elements: Using a credit or debit card
With knowledge that the card is stolen, revoked, or used without authorization
With intent to defraud
enhancements: Skimming device use: additional charges — MCL 750.157s
Organized fraud scheme: additional charges — MCL 750.218
Identity theft combined: concurrent charges
notes: Michigan credit card fraud governed by MCL 750.157m-157q. Skimming is separately criminalized. Restitution mandatory.

offense_class: Class F Felony ($1,000-$10,000); Class D Felony ($10,000+)
elements: Presenting, or causing to be presented
A claim for insurance benefits
Knowing the claim to contain materially false information
enhancements: Staged accident (auto insurance): additional charges
Healthcare fraud: federal prosecution possible
Multiple fraudulent claims: multiple counts
notes: Auto insurance fraud is prevalent in Michigan. Michigan also has specific auto no-fault fraud provisions. Workers' comp fraud under MCL 418.821.

offense_class: Class H Felony ($1,000-$20,000) to Class B Felony ($100,000+)
elements: Having property entrusted to one's care
By virtue of employment or position of trust
Fraudulent conversion of that property for own use
enhancements: Public official: mandatory restitution
Financial institution: enhanced penalties
Multiple victims: additional counts
notes: Michigan embezzlement has value-based tiers. Public official embezzlement may trigger additional penalties and forfeiture. Fiduciary breaches also subject to civil liability.

elements: Making a false statement or misrepresentation
In connection with an application for public assistance
With intent to fraudulently obtain benefits
enhancements: SNAP fraud: federal prosecution possible
Medicaid fraud: Class D Felony — MCL 400.606
Organized benefits fraud: enhanced charges
notes: Public assistance fraud covers food stamps (SNAP), TANF, Medicaid. Restitution and benefit ineligibility are common consequences. DHHS administrative sanctions run separately.

elements: Sexual penetration
With another person
Under circumstances set out in MCL 750.520b (age, force, coercion, incapacity, domestic relationship)
mandatory_minimum: 25-year mandatory minimum if victim under 13 at time of offense
enhancements: Victim under 13: mandatory 25-year minimum — MCL 750.520b(2)(b)
Multiple acts: consecutive sentencing
Prior CSC conviction: enhanced mandatory
Use of weapon or force: aggravating factor
notes: CSC-1 is Michigan's most serious sexual assault offense. Life or any term of years. Sex offender registration mandatory (Tier 3 — lifetime). Romeo and Juliet provisions do NOT apply to CSC-1.

elements: Sexual contact (not penetration)
With another person
Under circumstances described in MCL 750.520c
enhancements: Victim under 13: enhanced sentencing
Prior CSC conviction: significant enhancement
Use of weapon or threats: aggravating factor
notes: CSC-2 covers sexual contact (touching intimate parts). Tier 2 sex offender registration (25 years). Defenses include age proximity under MCL 750.520e.

elements: Sexual penetration
With another person
Under circumstances defined in MCL 750.520d (victim age 13-15, force, coercion, incapacity)
enhancements: Multiple acts: consecutive sentencing
Position of trust over victim: aggravating factor
Victim age 13-15 with actor 5+ years older: sex offender registration Tier 2
notes: CSC-3 involves penetration with victim aged 13-15 or involving force/coercion. Similar elements to CSC-1 but lesser circumstances. Sex offender registration required.

elements: Sexual contact
With another person
Under circumstances enumerated in MCL 750.520e (limited force, victim age, incapacity)
enhancements: Prior CSC conviction: Class D Felony
Position of authority: aggravating factor
Victim mental or physical incapacity: enhanced sentencing
notes: Highest-level misdemeanor CSC. Two-year Misdemeanor. Tier 1 sex offender registration (15 years). Romeo and Juliet exception if actor is less than 4 years older than 13-15 year old victim.

elements: Knowingly making any open or indecent exposure of person
Or of the person of another
In public or in a private place where others may see
enhancements: Fondling while exposing: Class H Felony — MCL 750.335a(2)(b)
Prior conviction: enhanced sentencing
In front of child: aggravating factor
notes: Aggravated indecent exposure (fondling while exposing) is a felony. Sex offender registration may be required depending on circumstances and prior record.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (93 days to 2 years depending on circumstances)
elements: Soliciting, enticing, or accosting another person
For the purpose of prostitution, lewdness, or assignation
In a public place or visible from a public place
enhancements: Soliciting a minor: Class D Felony — MCL 750.449a
Human trafficking: separate charges — MCL 750.462a
Using a vehicle: additional civil forfeiture
notes: Michigan's solicitation law. Johns may be charged under MCL 750.449a. Human trafficking prosecution increasingly common. Diversion programs available in some counties.

offense_class: Class B Felony (forced); Class C Felony (financial benefit)
elements: Recruiting, enticing, harboring, transporting, providing, obtaining, or maintaining a person
Through force, fraud, or coercion
For labor or commercial sexual activity
enhancements: Victim under 18: Class A Felony (Life) — MCL 750.462f
Victim under 13: enhanced mandatory
Use of controlled substance to facilitate: additional charges
notes: Michigan Human Trafficking Act (MCL 750.462a et seq.). Minor victims cannot consent — no defense of consent. Traffickers subject to asset forfeiture. SARO designation available to victims.

statute_title: Minor in Possession of Alcohol (MIP) / Disorderly Person
elements: Person under age 21
Possession, purchase, or consumption of alcohol
OR adult who is visibly intoxicated in public and creating a disturbance
enhancements: Using false ID to obtain alcohol: separate charge — MCL 436.1701
Furnishing alcohol to minor: Class A Misdemeanor — MCL 436.1701
Repeat offense: higher fine tier
notes: Michigan does not have a standalone public intoxication statute for adults. Adults charged under disorderly person statute (MCL 750.167). MIP is age-specific under Liquor Control Code.

elements: A person who is intoxicated in a public place and creates a disturbance
OR window peeper, brawler, loiterer for immoral purpose
OR engages in indecent, insulting, or obscene conduct
enhancements: Repeated disorderly conduct: sentencing enhancement
Combined with assault: separate charges
notes: Michigan's disorderly person statute covers numerous minor offenses. No separate 'disorderly conduct' statute — all under MCL 750.167. Civil infractions for minor disturbances.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (90 days) to Class E Felony (if armed)
elements: Entering or remaining upon property of another
Without permission
After being forbidden to do so
enhancements: Armed trespass: Class E Felony — MCL 750.552a
Critical infrastructure: enhanced felony
Prior trespass on same property: sentencing enhancement
notes: Simple trespass is 90-day misdemeanor. Trespass while armed is Class E Felony. Critical infrastructure trespass (pipelines, utilities) carries enhanced felony penalties.

statute_title: Resisting or Obstructing a Police Officer
offense_class: 2-year Misdemeanor; Class D Felony if injury
elements: Knowingly and willfully
Assault, batter, wound, resist, obstruct, oppose, or endanger
A person the defendant knows is performing official duties (law enforcement, EMT, firefighter)
enhancements: Officer injured: Class D Felony (up to 4 years)
Officer seriously injured: Class C Felony (up to 10 years)
Officer killed: Class B Felony (up to 20 years)
notes: Michigan's 'resisting and obstructing' is broader than resisting arrest — covers any interference with official duties. Verbal obstruction may suffice. Widely charged.

elements: An act or omission
That tends to impede or obstruct the administration of justice
With intent to obstruct
enhancements: Witness tampering: separate charge — MCL 750.122
Evidence destruction: separate charge — MCL 750.483a
Bribery of official: separate charge — MCL 750.117
notes: Michigan uses common law obstruction. Specific statutes for witness intimidation (MCL 750.122), jury tampering, and evidence destruction. False police report under MCL 750.411a.

elements: Making a false statement
Under oath in a judicial or quasi-judicial proceeding
With knowledge of falsity and intent to mislead
enhancements: False affidavit: MCL 750.423 (15 years)
Subornation of perjury: MCL 750.425 (5 years)
Perjury causing wrongful conviction: aggravating factor
notes: Michigan perjury carries up to 15 years — higher than many states. Subornation of perjury (procuring others to perjure) is a separate 5-year felony.

statute_title: Bribery of Public Officer or Employee
elements: Giving, offering, or promising
A benefit to a public officer or employee
With intent to influence their official action
enhancements: Receiving bribe (official): same penalties — MCL 750.118
Judicial bribery: enhanced
Commercial bribery: MCL 750.125 (1-year misdemeanor)
notes: Both giving and receiving bribery are separate offenses. Commercial bribery (private sector) is a misdemeanor. Kickback schemes may be charged as embezzlement or conspiracy.

elements: Conducting a financial transaction
Involving proceeds from a specified unlawful activity
With knowledge that the property represents proceeds of unlawful activity
With intent to conceal or disguise origin
enhancements: Federal money laundering concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 1956
Drug trafficking underlying: sentencing enhancement
Financial institution involved: additional penalties
notes: Michigan Money Laundering statute. Federal charges frequently concurrent. Asset forfeiture available. Structuring (avoiding reporting requirements) also chargeable.

statute_title: Michigan Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) — Conducting Criminal Enterprise
elements: A pattern of racketeering activity
Conducted through or in connection with an enterprise
With intent to benefit the enterprise
enhancements: Enterprise spanning multiple states: federal RICO concurrent
Murder predicate: enhanced sentencing
Leadership role: enhanced guidelines
notes: Michigan RICO under MCL 750.159f et seq. Forfeiture of enterprise assets. Civil RICO also available to plaintiffs. Requires 2+ related racketeering acts within 10 years.

statute_title: Street Gang Membership — Criminal Street Gang Activity
elements: Participation in a criminal street gang
By committing or attempting to commit a crime for the benefit of, at the direction of, or in association with the gang
enhancements: Crime near school: additional consecutive sentence
Crime involving firearms: enhanced penalties
Leadership: higher charge tier
notes: Michigan Criminal Street Gang statutes under MCL 750.411t et seq. Gang membership alone not criminal — must commit a crime for the gang. Sentencing enhancement for underlying crimes.

elements: Knowing and willful acts
As a condition or precondition of joining a group or organization
That involves physical harm, degradation, or endangerment
enhancements: Death resulting: manslaughter or murder charges
Serious injury: felony hazing — MCL 750.411t(1)(b)
Organizational officer involved: leadership enhancement
notes: Michigan Hazing Act covers schools, colleges, and organizations. 'Matt Araiza's Law' amendments. Organization may face civil and criminal liability.

offense_class: Revocation hearing; penalty up to maximum of underlying offense
elements: Defendant on probation
Willful violation of a probation condition
Established by preponderance of evidence at violation hearing
enhancements: Technical violation: judge has discretion — no statutory limit
New criminal offense: may result in maximum sentence
Absconding: warrant issued, detention pending hearing
notes: Michigan probation violations proceed before sentencing judge. No jury. Preponderance standard. Court can continue probation, modify conditions, or sentence to maximum. Technical violators may be eligible for Swift and Sure Sanctions program.

offense_class: Administrative proceeding; return to prison possible
elements: Parolee violating conditions of parole
Including new criminal conduct, absconding, or technical violations
enhancements: New felony while on parole: return to prison plus new sentence
Absconding: maximum penalty at hearing
notes: MDOC Parole Board has jurisdiction. Parole violations handled administratively. Parolee has due process rights (Morrissey v. Brewer). Michigan DOC may impose dipping, electronic monitoring, or return.

offense_class: Class G Felony (if convicted of felony); Misdemeanor (if awaiting trial on misdemeanor)
elements: Breaking from or escaping lawful custody
Of a prison, jail, or detention facility
OR escape from officer during transfer
enhancements: Use of force or weapon: additional assault charges
Escape by prisoner serving life: enhanced penalty
Multiple escape attempts: consecutive sentences
notes: MCL 750.193 covers escaping from custody of any confinement facility. Constructive escape (failure to return from work release) under MCL 800.74.

statute_title: False Report of a Felony or Misdemeanor
penalty_max: 93 days (minor false report); 4 years (false report of felony); additional if resources expended
elements: Knowing and wilful
Reporting to law enforcement a crime that did not occur
OR providing false information in a police report
enhancements: False bomb threat: Class D Felony — MCL 750.544
Resources expended in response: restitution mandatory
Terrorism false report: Class B Felony
notes: False felony report is Class F (4 years). False misdemeanor report is 93-day misdemeanor. Restitution for emergency response costs. False school bomb threat is separate enhanced offense.

elements: Intentionally and without authorization
Accessing, altering, damaging, or destroying
A computer program, network, or data
enhancements: Financial damage over $10,000: Class D Felony
Government systems: enhanced federal charges
Ransomware deployment: additional counts
notes: Michigan Computer Crime Law (MCL 752.791 et seq.). Federal CFAA charges frequently concurrent. Cyberbullying covered by separate statute (MCL 750.411x).

offense_class: Misdemeanor (93 days); Class E Felony if serious harm
penalty_max: 93 days; 1 year (2nd+); 5 years (bodily harm); Life (if death)
elements: Intentional posting of a message or statement
In a public media forum about a minor
Knowing the message is false, with intent to emotionally harm or extort
enhancements: Victim suffers serious bodily harm: Class E Felony
Victim commits suicide: Class B Felony or Life
Prior cyberbullying: 1-year misdemeanor
notes: Michigan's cyberbullying statute enacted 2018 (Matt Epling Law). Applies to minors. Adult cyberstalking under MCL 750.411h. Specific to false statements posted publicly about a minor.

statute_title: Obtaining Money by False Pretenses / Wire Fraud
offense_class: Class D Felony (state, $50,000+); federal: up to 20 years
elements: A scheme or artifice to defraud
Using electronic communications, wire, radio, or television
Obtaining money or property by false or fraudulent pretenses
enhancements: Financial institution as victim: 30 years federal
Emergency (disaster fraud): enhanced federal
Amounts over $1M: state Class C Felony
notes: State false pretenses under MCL 750.218; federal wire fraud under 18 U.S.C. § 1343. Federal prosecution typical for large schemes or interstate conduct.

statute_title: Tax Fraud / Failure to File — Michigan Income Tax
elements: Willful failure to file a required tax return
OR willful understatement or failure to pay taxes
With intent to evade tax obligation
enhancements: Fraudulent claim: enhanced penalties
Business/corporate tax fraud: corporate officer liability
Federal concurrent prosecution: IRS criminal division
notes: Michigan Treasury administers state tax fraud. Federal IRS charges frequently concurrent. Sales tax fraud (MCL 205.111) is separate.

elements: Malicious threats to extort money
OR threats to injure another's property, reputation, or person
With intent to compel compliance
enhancements: Amount extorted over $20,000: enhanced sentencing
Threat of violence: additional assault or terroristic threat charges
Use of computer/internet: cybercrime charges added
notes: Michigan extortion carries up to 20 years — more severe than many states. Blackmail (threatening exposure of information) falls under this statute. Separate from robbery.

offense_class: Class H Felony ($1,000+) to Class D Felony ($20,000+); Misdemeanor (under $1,000)
elements: Buying, receiving, possessing, or concealing stolen, embezzled, or converted property
With knowledge that it was stolen, embezzled, or converted
Intending to defraud the owner
enhancements: Organized auto theft ring: MCL 750.535a
Prior receiving stolen property conviction: sentencing enhancement
Commercial fencing operation: additional charges
notes: Value-based tiers same as larceny. Motor vehicle receiving stolen property enhanced under MCL 750.535(5). Proof of knowledge often circumstantial.

statute_title: Forgery of Public Records and Official Documents
elements: Fraudulently making, altering, or forging
A public record, official document, court record, instrument, or writing
With intent to defraud
enhancements: Uttering forged instrument: separate charge — MCL 750.249
Financial documents: enhanced penalties
Government document fraud: federal charges possible
notes: Michigan has multiple forgery statutes. MCL 750.248 (public records/court docs — 14 years), MCL 750.249 (private instruments — 14 years), MCL 750.250 (bank notes — 5 years). Uttering (using forged doc) is separate.

offense_class: Same maximum as the substantive offense conspired to commit
penalty_max: Same as underlying offense (Life if murder conspiracy)
elements: An agreement between two or more persons
To do an illegal act or a legal act in an illegal manner
With intent to commit the substantive offense
enhancements: Drug conspiracy: quantity-based thresholds apply
Federal conspiracy concurrent: 18 U.S.C. § 371
RICO conspiracy: additional enhancement
notes: Michigan conspiracy carries same maximum as the substantive offense. No overt act required for conspiracy in Michigan (split from federal law which requires overt act for § 371). Withdrawal defense possible.

offense_class: Reduced from substantive offense (generally 5 years max for felony, 2 years for misdemeanor)
penalty_max: 5 years for felony attempt; 2 years for misdemeanor attempt; Life if attempted murder
elements: Intent to commit a specific crime
AND an overt act done toward committing that crime
Falling short of completing the intended offense
enhancements: Attempted murder: assault with intent to murder — MCL 750.83 (Life)
Attempted armed robbery: Class C Felony
Near-completion of offense: sentencing enhancement
notes: Michigan attempt generally punished at reduced level. Attempted murder is separately codified as 'Assault with Intent to Murder' under MCL 750.83 (up to Life). General attempt statute MCL 750.92.

elements: The defendant assisted the principal
In the commission of the offense
With knowledge that the principal intended to commit a crime
AND intending to aid
enhancements: Active participation increases culpability
Weapon possession during aiding: felony firearm may attach
Getaway driver: same liability as principal
notes: Michigan law makes aiders and abettors equally guilty as principals. No separate 'accessory before the fact' distinction. Accessories after the fact are charged separately (MCL 750.505).

statute_title: Leaving the Scene of an Accident Involving Personal Injury or Death
offense_class: Class D Felony (injury); Class B Felony (death)
elements: Operating a motor vehicle involved in an accident
Resulting in injury or death to a person
Failing to stop, render aid, and provide information
enhancements: OWI at time of accident: concurrent charges
Death resulting: Class B Felony
Prior leaving scene: sentencing enhancement
notes: Duty to stop, render reasonable assistance, and provide identification. Property damage only: misdemeanor under MCL 257.618. Separate criminal culpability from underlying negligence.

statute_title: Vulnerable Adult Abuse — First Through Fourth Degree
offense_class: Class D Felony (1st); Class F Felony (2nd); Class H Felony (3rd); Misdemeanor (4th)
elements: A caregiver for a vulnerable adult
Intentionally or knowingly causes physical or mental harm
OR willful neglect of duty to provide care
enhancements: Financial exploitation concurrent: MCL 750.174a
Death of vulnerable adult: enhanced murder/manslaughter
Healthcare setting: licensing consequences
notes: Michigan Vulnerable Adults Act. 'Vulnerable adult' includes elderly or disabled persons under care. Mandatory reporting by caregivers. Financial exploitation of vulnerable adult is a separate offense.

statute_title: Financial Exploitation of a Vulnerable Adult
offense_class: Class D Felony ($1,000+) to Class C Felony ($100,000+)
elements: Obtaining money or property
From a vulnerable adult
Through undue influence, fraud, coercion, or breach of fiduciary duty
enhancements: Caregiver position of trust: sentencing enhancement
Embezzlement concurrent: MCL 750.174
Restitution mandatory
notes: Michigan's financial elder abuse statute. 'Vulnerable adult' includes those 18+ who are disabled or 65+ with limited capacity. Civil remedies also available (3x damages).

elements: Threatening to commit an act of terrorism
By any means of communication
With specific intent to terrorize
enhancements: Actual bomb/weapon present: terrorism execution charges — Class A
School threat: additional charges under school safety laws
Federal prosecution: 18 U.S.C. § 875 concurrent
notes: Michigan Anti-Terrorism Act (MCL 750.543b et seq.). School threats separately enhanced under MCL 750.543m and school safety laws. Causing evacuation (MCL 750.543p) is additional charge.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (up to 90 days) or higher depending on location
penalty_max: 90 days misdemeanor; felony if in school
elements: Carrying a pistol or dangerous weapon
Into a prohibited place
Without legal authority
enhancements: School zone: Class E Felony — MCL 750.237a
Courthouse: additional contempt charges
Legislative buildings: enhanced penalties
notes: Michigan's pistol-free zones include schools, courts, casinos, stadiums, hospitals. CPL holders not exempt from all zones (courts, polling places, churches by policy). School zone felony under MCL 750.237a.

offense_class: Class G Felony to Class E Felony
penalty_max: 2 years (possessing weapon at school); additional consecutive 2 years for crime in zone
elements: Possessing a dangerous weapon
On school property or in a vehicle on school property
Without school authorization
enhancements: Crime committed in school zone: mandatory 2-year consecutive sentence
Firearm involved: felony firearm may also attach
Pointing weapon at student: additional assault charges
notes: Weapon-free school zone enhancement adds consecutive 2 years for crimes committed with weapons in or near schools. Zero tolerance school discipline policies run separately.

statute_title: Bomb Threat / False Report of Explosive
elements: Making a false report or threat
Of a bomb, explosive, or other destructive device
Knowing the report is false or the threat is not real
enhancements: School bomb threat: separate enhanced provision under school safety
Resources expended: mandatory restitution
Multiple threats: additional counts
notes: False bomb threat is a felony in Michigan. Restitution for emergency response costs is mandatory. Juveniles frequently charged. Repeat school threats trigger habitual offender provisions.

statute_title: Animal Cruelty / Killing or Torturing an Animal
offense_class: Class H Felony (first); Class F Felony (repeat or extreme cruelty)
elements: Intentionally killing, maiming, or torturing an animal
OR using an animal in a fighting operation
OR abandonment causing death
enhancements: Animal fighting: Class H Felony — MCL 750.49
Second conviction: Class F Felony (4 years)
Cat or dog: enhanced penalties over other animals
notes: Michigan animal cruelty law enhanced 2007. Animal fighting is separately criminalized. Domestic violence animal abuse connection often used in prosecution strategy.

elements: Two or more persons acting in concert
Committing retail fraud
With total value exceeding $1,000
enhancements: Organized retail theft ring: MCL 752.1081 enhanced penalties
Prior retail fraud: degree enhancement
Fraud device used: additional charges
notes: Organized retail fraud creates felony liability where individual thefts might be misdemeanors. Michigan Organized Retail Crime Act (MCL 752.1081 et seq.) provides additional enforcement.

statute_title: Assaulting, Battering, Wounding, Resisting, or Obstructing Officer
elements: Assaulting, battering, wounding, resisting, obstructing, opposing, or endangering
A person the defendant knows or has reason to know is performing official duties
Including law enforcement, EMTs, corrections officers, firefighters
enhancements: Officer seriously injured: Class C Felony
Officer killed: Class B Felony
Use of weapon: felony firearm may apply
notes: MCL 750.81d covers broad category of interference with officers and emergency responders. Even verbal obstruction may qualify. Enhanced penalties scale with resulting harm.

statute_title: Fleeing and Eluding — Operating Vehicle to Avoid Police
offense_class: Class G Felony (1st); Class F Felony (2nd); Class D Felony (3rd/4th)
penalty_max: 2 years (1st); 4 years (2nd); 10 years (3rd/4th with injury or reckless driving)
elements: Operating a motor vehicle
Willfully failing to obey a police officer's signal to stop
While the officer is in uniform and the vehicle is marked
enhancements: Sustained high-speed chase: 3rd degree — Class F
Causing injury or extreme recklessness: 4th degree — Class D
Prior fleeing conviction: degree enhancement
notes: Michigan has four degrees of fleeing and eluding. 1st degree (2 years) is base, escalating with risk factors. Combined with OWI or reckless driving in many cases.

offense_class: 2-year Misdemeanor (simple); up to Class C Felony (injury)
penalty_max: 2 years (intimidation); escalates based on underlying crime
elements: Malicious use of violence, property damage, or harassment
Motivated by the victim's race, color, religion, gender, or national origin
With intent to intimidate or harm
enhancements: Underlying assault: combined sentencing
Bias-motivated property destruction: mandatory sentencing enhancement
Multiple victims targeted: additional counts
notes: Michigan Ethnic Intimidation Act (MCL 750.147b). Does not include sexual orientation (gap in Michigan law as of writing). Civil remedies under Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act also available.

elements: Recruiting, harboring, transporting, providing, or obtaining a person
By force, fraud, or coercion
For the purpose of forced labor or services
enhancements: Victim under 18: Class A Felony — MCL 750.462f
Use of controlled substance to facilitate: additional charges
Leadership role: enhanced sentencing
notes: Michigan Human Trafficking Act (MCL 750.462a et seq.). Civil cause of action available to victims (MCL 750.462n). Asset forfeiture. Federal parallel prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 1589.

elements: Manufacturing, possessing, transporting, or delivering
Any explosive or incendiary device
Without lawful authority or license
enhancements: Intent to terrorize: Class B Felony under MCL 750.543n
Used in crime: additional charges
Near school: mandatory consecutive enhancement
notes: Michigan explosives possession statute. Licensed mining/commercial use exempt. Molotov cocktails and improvised explosive devices clearly covered. Federal concurrent prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 844.

elements: Pretending to be a peace officer or public official
Without lawful authority
While exercising authority claimed from that position
enhancements: Assault or fraud committed while impersonating: additional charges
Use of official-looking badge/vehicle: sentencing enhancement
Traffic stop impersonation: enhanced penalties
notes: Using a fake badge or wearing law enforcement uniform while acting as officer. Separate from impersonating public employees (MCL 750.217). High-profile cases involve fake traffic stops.

penalty_max: 93 days (indefinite for civil contempt until compliance)
elements: Willful disobedience of a court order
OR conduct that disrupts, obstructs, or interferes with judicial proceedings
enhancements: Contempt of PPO: also criminal charge under MCL 600.2950
Repeated contempt: multiple consecutive counts
Jury present: direct contempt — immediate sanction
notes: Michigan contempt is 93 days per count, but multiple counts can stack. Civil contempt for compliance continues until defendant complies. Criminal contempt for past conduct ends with sentence.

elements: Knowingly restraining another person
Under circumstances that do not amount to kidnapping
Without legal authority and without consent
enhancements: Kidnapping (if all elements met): Class A Felony — MCL 750.349
Victim is minor: enhanced sentencing
Use of force or weapon: additional charges
notes: Lesser offense to kidnapping. No specific intent to ransom or harm required. Used when kidnapping cannot be proven. Often charged with other offenses.

offense_class: Class E Felony to Class B Felony (amount-based)
elements: Making a materially false statement
In connection with a mortgage loan application or real estate transaction
With intent to defraud a lender or purchaser
enhancements: Multiple loan applications: multiple counts
Bank fraud: federal prosecution concurrent
Real estate professional involved: licensing action
notes: Michigan Mortgage Fraud Act. Straw buyer arrangements and appraisal fraud commonly charged. Federal bank fraud under 18 U.S.C. § 1344 frequently concurrent.

offense_class: Civil infraction to Misdemeanor; Felony for large-scale dumping
elements: Knowingly depositing solid waste
On property without authorization
Other than a licensed waste disposal facility
enhancements: Hazardous waste: enhanced felony — MCL 324.11122
Large volume (7+ cubic yards): Class G Felony
Corporate dumping: officer liability
notes: Regulated under Michigan Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act. Hazardous waste dumping is separately enhanced. Local ordinance violations run concurrently.

elements: A person intoxicated by alcohol or a controlled substance
In a public place
Creating a disturbance or unable to care for self
enhancements: Repeat offender: diversion/treatment may be required
Combined with DV or assault: separate charges
notes: Michigan does not have a standalone drunk in public statute. Charged under the disorderly person statute. Typical resolution is a fine with community service. Treatment courts available.

elements: Willful and malicious conduct
In disruption of a lawful assembly or public peace
OR using profane or indecent language in public
enhancements: Near school or church: local ordinance enhancement
Repeat conduct: sentencing enhancement
notes: Michigan disturbing the peace under MCL 750.167. Most jurisdictions also have local noise ordinances as civil infraction alternative. First Amendment considerations apply to pure speech.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (2 years); Class E Felony if aggravated
elements: A willful course of conduct
Involving repeated electronic communications
That would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, or harassed
enhancements: Violation of PPO: aggravated — MCL 750.411t
Prior stalking conviction: aggravated charge
Victim under 18: aggravated stalking
notes: Michigan's electronic stalking statute under MCL 750.411s. Different from cyberbullying (MCL 750.411x) which targets minors specifically. 'Course of conduct' requires 2+ acts.

elements: Stalking (course of conduct causing reasonable fear)
PLUS: violation of PPO, prior stalking conviction, victim under 18, or making credible threat
enhancements: Prior aggravated stalking: enhanced sentencing
Use of weapon: additional charges
Child victim: sex offender registration if elements met
notes: Aggravated stalking requires base stalking plus one aggravating factor. PPO violation concurrent with stalking creates presumptive aggravated charge. Sex offender registration may apply if victim is minor.

elements: Willfully communicating with a juror
In relation to the juror's duties
With intent to influence a verdict or decision
enhancements: Bribery of juror: additional bribery charges — MCL 750.120
Organized tampering scheme: conspiracy charges
During capital case: enhanced sentencing
notes: Juror tampering includes contact with juror or potential juror. Obstruction of justice may also be charged concurrently. Social media contact with jurors increasingly prosecuted.

statute_title: Intimidation of a Witness or Victim
offense_class: Class F Felony (4 years); Class C Felony (15 years) if serious harm
penalty_max: 4 years (intimidation only); 15 years (if serious injury results)
elements: Intimidating, interfering with, or bribing a witness or victim
With intent to obstruct justice or prevent testimony
In a pending or prospective criminal proceeding
enhancements: Assault of witness: additional charges and enhanced sentencing
Gang-related intimidation: gang enhancement
Prior witness tampering: habitual offender sentencing
notes: Victim intimidation and witness tampering are combined under MCL 750.122. Serious injury to witness elevates to Class C Felony. Applies to prospective (not just pending) proceedings.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (93 days to 2 years depending on circumstances)
elements: Engaging in sexual acts
For hire or compensation
With another person
enhancements: Near school: enhanced penalties
HIV positive and engaging in prostitution: felony — MCL 333.5210
Trafficking component: Class B/C Felony — MCL 750.462a
notes: Michigan's prostitution laws apply to both selling and buying sex. Prior to 2023 reforms, sellers faced more enforcement than buyers. Human trafficking laws increasingly used for exploitation cases.

elements: Procuring, inducing, or enticing a person
To become a prostitute or to engage in sexual acts for hire
Through persuasion, promises, threats, or violence
enhancements: Victim under 18: Class B Felony (human trafficking) — MCL 750.462f
Violence used: additional assault charges
Drug use to control victim: additional charges
notes: Pandering (procuring) and keeping a house of prostitution (MCL 750.452) are separate offenses. Human trafficking charges increasingly used for exploitation of adults and minors.

statute_title: Possession of Child Sexually Abusive Material (CSAM)
elements: Knowingly possessing
Any child sexually abusive material
Knowing or having reason to know it is child sexually abusive material
enhancements: Production or distribution: Class B or C Felony — MCL 750.145c(2)/(3)
Using a computer to distribute: enhanced federal charges
Prior CSAM conviction: enhanced sentencing
notes: Michigan uses 'child sexually abusive material' (CSAM). Production is Class B Felony (20 years). Distribution is Class C Felony (7 years). Tier 3 sex offender registration (lifetime). Federal parallel prosecution common.

statute_title: Production of Child Sexually Abusive Material (CSAM)
elements: Persuading, inducing, enticing, coercing, or forcing a child
To engage in sexually explicit conduct
For the purpose of producing child sexually abusive material
enhancements: Child under 13: enhanced federal prosecution
Prior CSAM conviction: mandatory enhancement
Distribution of material: additional Class C Felony count
notes: Most serious CSAM offense in Michigan. Life sentences available for repeat offenders. Federal prosecution under 18 U.S.C. § 2251 typically concurrent. Tier 3 sex offender registration mandatory.

statute_title: OWI with Passenger Under 16 Years of Age
elements: Operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated
With a passenger under 16 years of age in the vehicle
enhancements: Child protective services referral mandatory
Enhanced sentence on primary OWI charge
Repeat offense: child endangerment charges possible
notes: Separate misdemeanor charge in addition to primary OWI. Child Protective Services will be notified. License suspension includes this factor. Second offense with child present escalates severity.
